To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the critical velocity for the attachment of two spherical particles during impact can be predicted by the critical velocity model, which is based on the Hertz contact theory, and the sticking efficiency can be improved by adjusting the vibration velocity of the carrier.
the critical velocity for particle adhesion is determined, and the optimal vibration parameters to maximize the number of particles attaching to a carrier are identified.

a discrete element method can be used to investigate the adhesive interactions between API particles and carrier particles and the optimal amplitude and frequency can be found for the vibration velocity in order to maximise the number and sticking efficiency of the API particles adhering on the carrier.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the adhesive behaviour between two particles and between fine particles and a large carrier in the process of powder mixing for DPI formulation development.

the particle-particle interactions in a DPI, including the adhesive interactions and the particle adhesion to a large carrier during powder mixing, which is critical for the formulation and manufacturing process development of DPIs.
the fundamental adhesive interactions between particles in a DPI, which is important for the development of DPI formulation and process design.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact number, detachment number and sticking efficiency are all dependent on the amplitude and frequency of the vibration process.
the optimal vibration velocity can maximise the contact number and sticking efficiency.
the optimal vibration velocity is the velocity that maximises the contact number.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a critical velocity criterion for adhesive particle rebound is developed, the optimal vibration velocity for the attachment process is identified and the effect of vibration parameters on the attachment process is quantitatively evaluated.

the critical velocity criterion is a good indicator to evaluate the adhesion of two autoadhesive spherical elastic particles, the optimal amplitude and frequency are important for the attachment of small API particles to a large carrier, and the vibration velocity can be used to control the adhesion between particles.
the DEM model is a useful tool for understanding particle attachment and detachment processes in DPIs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the discrete element method (DEM) can be used to study particle adhesion in powder mixing processes and the critical velocity criterion can be used to determine the impact velocity required for particle adhesion.
the discrete element method can be employed as a useful tool for the development of DPI formulations.

the DEM method can be employed to simulate and understand the particle adhesion and detachment processes in DPIs and the proposed critical velocity criterion can be used to predict the adhesion probability between two autoadhesive particles during their impact.
